summary: The ladder starts with September's gross revenue against August, shows that the fall hit every store, separates fewer orders per day from a smaller average order caused by fewer jaffles, and ends by sizing three levers: jaffle sales, each store's jaffle share and average order.

narration.text: September 2026 gross revenue was $208.0K, down 13.4% on August.
The drop was not confined to one café, since all four stores sold less than in August, with Brooklyn down 14.9% to $93.0K and Philadelphia down 14.7% to $57.3K.
Chicago fell the least at 8.0% and San Francisco slipped 11.4%.
Set against the year so far, September still sits well above the same month last year, and the dip follows an August peak of $240.4K.
The fall came from both fewer orders and a smaller average order: orders per day dropped from 686.7 in August to 644.8 in September, while the average order slipped from $11.29 to $10.75.
Jaffles drove the smaller basket, as units sold fell 20.5% against 8.8% for beverages.
Every store saw its average order shrink, with Brooklyn down from $10.96 to $10.38, and Brooklyn and Philadelphia also lost the most daily orders.
Start by winning back jaffle sales, beginning with Nutellaphone who dis?, which fell 26.3% in units to 1,188, the steepest drop of the five jaffles.
Raise the jaffle share of each store's units towards Chicago's 23.2%, since Brooklyn sits at 21.1% and San Francisco at 20.5%.
Test ways to lift the average order in trailing stores, as Brooklyn at $10.38 and San Francisco at $10.61 sit below Chicago's $11.28.

The best levers are winning back jaffle sales, starting with Nutellaphone who dis?, lifting jaffle share towards Chicago's 23.2%, and raising the average order in stores trailing Chicago's $11.28.
